tweets: GLP-1 agonists like semaglutide are widely discussed now — understanding their clinical use requires careful physician oversight and patient safety measures. We're building a telehealth practice focused on these principles for peptide therapies.

Peptide therapies require clinical supervision to ensure appropriate use and monitoring. Our model emphasizes careful clinician review to assess if peptide therapy fits each patient's unique health profile.
The evidence for many peptides includes some human data but remains preliminary. We prioritize clinician evaluation to guide decisions based on individual health status and lab results.
We're building a telehealth model where US-licensed physicians asynchronously review labs, monitor progress, and adjust treatment plans — not a quick prescription or refill service.
Our practice will use 503A-compounded peptides only, avoiding research-use-only products. This approach supports quality and compliance with regulatory standards when we launch.
Peptides are not FDA-approved medications. Suitability and prescribing decisions will be made by licensed clinicians based on individual clinical assessment and lab results.
